item.title: How Mara is reshaping Afrobeats
item.description: The ‘Mara’ sub-genre has quietly become one of the most kinetic forces shaping Afrobeats, rooted in the street cultures of Mainland Lagos, Nigeria. Defined by fast-paced beats, dramatic sound effects, and legwork-heavy dance styles, Mara reflects everyday urban energy and humor. item.title: Museum exhibit spotlights Africa’s lost artifacts
item.description: Manchester Museum has unveiled thousands of African artifacts while openly acknowledging it knows “little to nothing” about the origins of many of them. Displayed in the new Africa Hub, the objects—collected during the British Empire through trade, conquest, and looting—highlight missing histories rather than polished narratives. item.description: Israel has given final approval to a $37 billion deal to increase natural gas exports to Egypt. item.title: Uganda’s export earnings soar
item.description: Uganda’s export earnings surged in October, nearly doubling from a year earlier as higher global prices lifted revenues from key commodities. According to the finance ministry, merchant goods exports climbed to $1.5 billion, up sharply from about $770 million in October 2024. item.title: Diageo to exit East African Breweries
item.description: Diageo is set to exit East Africa after agreeing to sell its entire 65% stake in East African Breweries (EABL) for $2.3 billion. The buyer, Japan’s beverage group Asahi, will take control if the deal receives regulatory approval. This move concludes a strategic review of Diageo’s East African business and marks its second major divestment on the […]
